did_you_know.text: Did you know? Solomon is described here as king over all Israel, emphasizing the extent of his reign and his rule over the united kingdom.
Did you know? The royal administration included a variety of officials: priests, scribes, a secretary, the commander of the army, the palace administrator, and the official in charge of forced labor.
Did you know? Solomon had twelve district governors, each responsible for providing food for the king and his household for one month of the year.
Did you know? The list of governors shows that the land was divided administratively into districts, including the hill country of Ephraim, Shaalbim, Arubboth, and the region of Dor.
Did you know? Baana son of Ahilud was responsible for Taanach, Megiddo, and the area of Beth-shean, extending as far as Abel-meholah and Jokmeam.
Did you know? Ben-geber was responsible for Ramoth-gilead. His district included the region of Argob and the settlements of Jair, as well as sixty large fortified cities with walls and bronze bars.
Did you know? Ahimaaz, who was governor over Naphtali, married Basemath, Solomon’s daughter. This indicates a marriage connection between the royal family and one of the officials.
Did you know? Geber son of Uri was in charge of the land of Gilead, described as the former land of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan. One governor was also in the land alongside him.
Did you know? The text summarizes the people’s condition in Solomon’s time by describing their great number—as numerous as the sand on the seashore—and their eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
